question: Can one hidden Boolean-q wire D realize a reusable ALL_EQ_3 fanout on named outputs A,B,C while leaving at least three ports free on each named output for a minimum direct OR_3 occurrence?

bounded_language.splice_edges: all 216 cross-wire port pairs between distinct wires
bounded_language.port_capacity: matching: each exposed endpoint is used at most once
bounded_language.source_open_gate: the three initial H paths per wire plus selected splice edges remain a disjoint union of open paths; any edge closing a path component into an H cycle is rejected
bounded_language.local_semantics: exact v8.2 affine F3 boundary state (c,s,q), q in {+1,-1}
bounded_language.frame_quotient: fix A to (c,s)=(0,+1) by global AGL(1,3)=S3 colour symmetry; enumerate all 6^3=216 frames for B,C,D for each q tuple
bounded_language.hidden_projection: existentially quantify both q_D and D's affine frame

completeness_argument: The edge universe contains every cross-wire pair of the six exposed ports on each of four wires: C(4,2)*6*6 = 216 candidate splice edges.
DFS chooses edge indices in strictly increasing order, so every unordered candidate edge set is represented once before physical pruning.

The dynamic path-partner state is an exact representation of a disjoint union of open H paths. An unused endpoint may be spliced to another unused endpoint; if the two are already opposite endpoints of the same current path, that splice would close an H cycle and is rejected. Otherwise the two paths concatenate and their remaining endpoints become partners.
Named and hidden load bounds are checked before every splice. Because each selected edge consumes exactly one port at each endpoint wire, these checks are exact for the stated interface budget.

For every one of the 16 q tuples, the checker carries a 216-bit exact set of surviving B,C,D affine frames after globally fixing A. Adding a splice intersects this set with that edge's exact colour-inequality mask; therefore semantic states only disappear as DFS depth increases.

The only semantic prune requires the +++ and --- named branches each to remain nonempty after existential q_D projection. This prune is monotone-safe: a final ALL_EQ_3 relation must contain both branches, and later edge intersections cannot restore a branch once eliminated.
The target relation is tested before the depth-7 cutoff, so gadgets of every size 1 through 7 are included.

theorem.name: ONE_HIDDEN_WIRE_REUSABLE_Q_FANOUT_IS_BLOCKED_THROUGH_SEVEN_SPLICES_IN_THE_EXACT_V8_2_LANGUAGE
theorem.statement: Within the exact four-wire v8.2 Boolean-q splice language, with one hidden wire D, source-open topology, matching port use, named loads at most three, hidden load at most six, and at most seven cross-wire splice edges, existential elimination of D never yields exactly ALL_EQ_3 on A,B,C.
theorem.scope_warning: This is a finite bounded-language barrier only. It does not exclude two or more hidden wires, larger splice budgets paired with different clause interfaces, non-direct clause gadgets, different local carriers, or other encodings.

next_target.name: E8_V8_4_INDEPENDENT_REPLAY_AND_V8_5_MINIMAL_AUXILIARY_ESCALATION
next_target.directive: First replay v8.4 with an independently implemented source-open test/state engine. If the same exact negative result is reproduced, seal v8.4. Then escalate minimally: determine whether two hidden q wires can realize a source-open reusable ALL_EQ_3 fanout under a rigorously derived finite port/splice budget, rather than relaxing all bounds at once.
